props.label: NEW README
props.title: Snippet-first root README
props.subtitle: Six sections, ~60 lines. The paste block is the product; everything else frames it.

props.title: README outline
props.content:
**1. Title + one line.** "Agent-agnostic CLI for AI-assisted development. It installs a shared set of SDLC skills onto your machine so your coding agent runs the same plan → execute → review workflow everyone else does." No mission statement.

**2. Set up — the copy-paste block** (below), introduced by a single line: *Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or whatever agent you use.* Followed by three requirement lines (git, Node 20+, npm on PATH; Bitbucket SSH; `ULTA_HOME=<path>` to install elsewhere) and one pointer: *if either command fails, the error names a section in docs/installation.md.*

**3. Daily use** — literal prompts, since that is what the user types: *"Use jira-ingest on ULTA-1234"*, *"Use planning to turn that into an implementation plan"*, *"Use execute"*, *"Use review"*. Plus `ulta skill list --global` for the full set — a real command (surface-registry.js:486-502) that replaces the dead lifecycle cross-reference.

**4. Where things land** — four rows, no prose: `.ulta/user/` (git-ignored), `~/.config/ulta/config.yaml`, `~/.agents/skills/`, `~/.local/share/ulta-ai-cli`.

**5. Update** — corrected, not copied forward: `ulta update` is the path. Re-running install.sh from inside the clone does **not** pull new commits (verified: install.sh:19-23 sets the in-place flag and :126-136 returns before any fetch). `ulta update --bulletin` shows what changed; `--verify` checks it applied.

**6. More** — five one-line links: `ulta --help`, installation, skills, config spec, AGENTS.md.

**Dropped:** the 54-line mermaid diagram, rollout model, Context Engine relationship, the hand-maintained command reference (`ulta --help` is generated and cannot go stale), capability and limitation decks, audience routing.

Install the Ulta AI CLI on this machine and onboard me.

1. Run these two commands:
   git clone git@bitbucket.org:ulta-beauty/ulta-ai-cli.git \
     ~/.local/share/ulta-ai-cli
   ~/.local/share/ulta-ai-cli/install.sh

2. The installer's last line is a path to an
   onboarding/SKILL.md. Read that file and
   follow it end to end.

3. Tell me what it recorded as complete and
   what it reported as skipped.

props.label: CONVERSATION LEAKAGE
props.title: Worst offenders
props.subtitle: Prose that explains decisions, narrates history, or parks meeting state — invisible to a fresh reader, corrosive to trust.

props.content: "6) Immediate next steps (JP)" — docs/guides/ulta-alignment-questions.md. The entire file is a nine-line meeting agenda with an assignee's initials, filed as documentation. Its answer sheet is a second file.

"Known Gaps and Roadmap — direct fetch is gated on tracker MCP availability (official DSP OAuth client pending)… DAG parallelism is unit-tested but unproven in production" — docs/lifecycle.md:262-271. Internal procurement state and backlog inside a doc labeled an enterprise contract.
"graph building is being reworked on a separate thread. Until that lands, this skill still emits the legacy artifacts." — graph-ontology/SKILL.md:10. The only leakage that ships to user machines.

props.title: The pattern, by tier
props.content:
**Tier 1 — files that are entirely conversation:** the alignment agenda and its answer sheet; the three dated business-context plan memos (executive-briefing headers, unchecked task boxes, a hard-coded "all 36 tests pass"); the service-agents retrospective ("The Five Refactoring Corrections Applied" — a PR ledger with no referent for a fresh reader).

**Tier 2 — roadmap ledgers inside reference docs:** the lifecycle doc's known-gaps section; the config spec's "Board Review Topics" — three unresolved decisions parked in a spec, awaiting a meeting.

**Tier 3 — rationale and history where behavior belongs:** installation.md narrating a pending npm-link decision and carrying a TODO addressed to a future maintainer; before/after blocks written for a reviewer of a past commit; skills.md announcing that rsync is "no longer required" — a changelog entry about a dependency the current reader never had; the lifecycle doc's unsourced 3× speedup benchmark crediting Netty in a Node child-process spawn; the README's "System Limitations" evaluation-deck framing whose specific claims describe code that does not exist.

props.title: Ordered execution plan

items.title: Source fixes that unblock deletions
items.content: Repoint runtime doc refs before any file moves: the generic-primer ref → skills.md (and fix --agent → --skill in the repair string); 58 governance refs → skills.md; 3 quickstart refs → README.md; layering-standard links → the config spec. Add the missing #list/#sync anchors. File — separately — the phantom-spec refs and stale curl|bash strings.

items.title: Content merges (before deleting sources)
items.content: quickstart → new README per the outline. Governance flowchart → skills.md (and fix the rules path). Migration-guide troubleshooting table → the writing-skills skill. The three development docs' unique parts → getting-started-dev.md. Layering precedence table → the config spec. Commit convention → AGENTS.md.

items.title: Deletions
items.content: 22 doc files, four whole directories (development, designs, plans, confluence), CONTRIBUTING.md, both drawio files, and the three empty skill shells (tdd, dead-code, repo-onboarding).

items.title: Fix the survivors
items.content: installation.md (cut 3 blocks, fix 8 claims), skills.md (fix flags, thin promote to CLI mechanics, drop leakage), getting-started-dev.md (drop the invented error code, complete the command table), cli-architecture.md (module ownership + registry modules), config spec (defaults block), AGENTS.md (archive pointer, deploy block), CHANGELOG (backfill 2.1.0).

items.title: Verify + guard
items.content: pnpm test:all — two suites assert getting-started-dev.md resolves on disk, catching a wrong delete. Then add the guard test that greps every runtime docs_ref and confirms each target file and anchor exists — the one check that would have caught all four phantom specs and both dead anchors, and the only thing preventing this class of rot from returning.
